messages.subject: Seasobal model
parts:
Hi,

I need to fit the temporal model with the seasonal effect. I have annual data which has four seasons  (aggregated annual data for four seasons). 

1. What is the best way to use seasonal effect in R-INLA

2. I need to compare Poisson and NB models using measure of fit/goodness of fit test. Even DIC and WAIC are low in Poisson, is there a way to prove the goodness of fit for this?
.

Thank you

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Seasobal model
parts:
If you have four seasons, s=1,2,3,4, say, then you could either use
factor, as

s.fac = as.factor(s)

. ~ ... + s.fac

if you want to impose spatial dependency, then you can use

. ~ ... + f(s, model="rw2", cyclic=TRUE, scale.model=TRUE)

if the effects of the seasons also vary with time, then you can use
model="seasonal", see inla.doc("seasonal")


you'll likelly need do compare the saturated dic/waic as the likelihood
changes. alternative, is to use proper priors and compare the marginal
likelihood.

H
